newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products up with crude, good demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products up with crude, good demand.

text.p: Singapore oil products rose on Friday on firmer crude values and strong North Asian demand, traders said.

"Regional jet fuel supplies are starting to look tight," one trader said. Prices rose substantially as winter demand from North Asia finally kicked in, traders said. A major was bidding for 120,000-barrels at $32.30 a barrel, lifting fob Singapore early December, up 35 cents from Thursday's traded level - already a post-winter record. A 100,000-barrel-lot was traded late Thursday at $31.95, up 20 cents from the previous post-winter high chalked up a day earlier.
The December jet fuel/gas oil spread also firmed to trade at $1.72 and was quoted at $1.60/$1.90, up 30 cents from Thursday.

Gas oil also firmed despite initial bearish talks on Friday morning when the market halved its expectations of India's January purchase to 350,000-tonnes. Results of the tender which closed November 21 are due late Friday.

But a stronger IPE open, with December gas oil futures up $5.00 a tonne to $224.00, and sustained buying from China kept prices firm. Cargoes were bid at $31.00 a barrel, up 10 cents from Thursday. December swaps rose late afternoon to trade at an intra-day high of $30.60, from Thursday's $30.40/$30.60.

Naphtha firmed on bullish sentiment arising from good North Asian demand. Traders said the naphtha/gasoline spread, assessed around $2.00 a barrel was likely to narrow on the strength of naphtha. Naphtha December swaps rose to $23.55/$23.70 from $22.70/$22.85 on Thursday, with January in a steep 60-cent backwardation. Gasoline traders were quiet with buyers seeking further direction from Taiwan's buy tender for January 1-15 which closes Monday.
